title: Retrieval (RAG)
blurb: How chatbots answer from your documents by looking things up first.

slides.title: Give the model the right pages to read
body: A model doesn’t know your organisation’s documents, and its knowledge stops at a cut-off date.
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) fixes that by searching your documents first, then putting the most relevant passages into the context window alongside the question.

visual.caption: The retrieved passages take up much of the window, so the answer can come from them.

slides.title: How a RAG system answers
body: It all happens in the moment a question arrives. The model itself isn’t changed.
The search step often uses embeddings, so it finds passages by meaning rather than exact words.

visual.caption: Search, then answer — every time a question comes in.

items.label: 1. Search
items.text: Find the passages most relevant to the question.

items.label: 2. Add to context
items.text: Put those passages into the prompt with the question.

items.label: 3. Answer
items.text: The model answers from the passages — ideally saying which ones it used.

slides.title: Why it helps
body: RAG is one of the most common ways organisations use AI with their own information.

visual.caption: Benefits depend on good documents and good search.

items.heading: Up to date
items.text: Update the documents and answers change too — no retraining.

items.heading: Your own knowledge
items.text: Answers can draw on internal documents the model never saw.

items.heading: Checkable
items.text: Each answer can point to the passage it came from.

items.heading: Less guessing
items.text: Made-up answers become less likely, though not impossible.

slides.title: Where it goes wrong
body: A RAG system is only as good as its search. If the right passage isn’t found, the model can’t use it — and may answer anyway.
Most problems can be traced to one of these.

visual.caption: When a RAG answer is wrong, check what was retrieved first.

items.heading: Wrong passages found
items.text: The search misses the relevant text, or finds something similar but wrong.

items.heading: Chopped-up documents
items.text: Documents are split into chunks, and a key point can be cut in half.

items.heading: Passages misread
items.text: The model can still misunderstand the source or mix in outside knowledge.

quiz.question: What does a RAG system add before the model answers?
options: Relevant passages found by searching a document collection
A second model to check spelling
quiz.explanation: RAG retrieves relevant passages and adds them to the context, so the model can answer from them.

quiz.question: An internal policy changes. How does a RAG system pick up the new version?
options: The model has to be retrained from scratch
Update the document in the collection it searches
It finds out automatically from the news
It can’t — RAG only works with fixed documents
quiz.explanation: Because answers come from the documents at question time, updating the documents is enough.

quiz.question: A RAG chatbot gives a wrong answer. What’s a common cause?
options: The search found the wrong passages, or missed the right one
quiz.explanation: If the right information doesn’t reach the context, the model can’t use it — and may fill the gap with a guess.
